sections.h2: What is St. Clair County, Illinois, and who bills the property tax?
sections.html:
St. Clair County sits directly east of St. Louis in the Metro East region, where Belleville is both the seat of government and the biggest city. The county board, assessor, board of review, treasurer and county clerk each handle one piece of the property tax, so a homeowner usually talks to more than one office. The Assessor sets the value, the Board of Review hears appeals, the County Clerk calculates the rate and the Treasurer collects the bill.

The county is large: 674 square miles in total, of which 658 are land, and it holds East St. Louis, Belleville, O'Fallon, Fairview Heights, Mascoutah, Lebanon, Cahokia Heights, Madison and parts of Collinsville and Columbia. Four interstates cross it (I-55, I-64, I-70 and I-255), eleven MetroLink stations serve it, and Scott Air Force Base is inside the county line. Cahokia was settled by French colonists in 1697, and the county was created in 1790, making it the first county established in what is now Illinois.

A seller needs the Treasurer's payment history, the assessor's property record card and a clear plan for how taxes will be split at closing. This page covers each in turn.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for housing in St. Clair County?
sections.html:
St. Clair County has a population estimate of 250,708 for July 1, 2025, down from 257,400 at the 2020 census. A typical owned home is valued at $180,300 and typical rent is $1,090, and 68.4% of homes have an owner living in them. Household income at the midpoint is $73,854, and 12.7% of residents are below the poverty line (Census QuickFacts, 2020-2024).

Owning costs $1,645 a month at the midpoint for mortgage holders and $645 for owners with no loan. There are 100,846 households, and the average household has 2.47 people. These numbers vary widely between Belleville, the Scott AFB area and East St. Louis, so use them as a county-wide reference and look at sales on your own street.

sections.h2: When are St. Clair County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes for one year are billed and paid in the next, in two installments. The Treasurer's published schedule for 2025 taxes payable in 2026 is below, and it marked every date as tentative. All of those dates have now passed, so ask the Treasurer's office for the schedule that applies to the next bill.

St. Clair County Treasurer collection dates, 2025 taxes payable in 2026

Source: St. Clair County Treasurer, Collection Dates. The counter closes at 4:30 p.m. and opens at 8:30 a.m. Electronic payments stop at 3 p.m. on the last day to avoid publication and on the last day to pay, and a postmark is not accepted for those deadlines.

sections.h2: What happens if a tax bill is paid late or not at all?
sections.html:
The State of Illinois imposes a 1.5% monthly penalty on the unpaid balance of a late installment, and the penalty grows by another 1.5% every thirty days. The amount owed with penalty is printed on each payment coupon. Partial payments can only be taken by the Treasurer's Office, not by the collector banks.

Unpaid tax can lead to a sale of the lien. The Treasurer states that an owner keeps the right to redeem for two and one-half years when the property is a principal dwelling with no more than six apartment units, and for two years on other property. Redemption costs the tax plus penalties and interest, and failing to redeem can mean losing the property. For a home with delinquent taxes, a seller should arrange to pay the balance at closing, and the buyer's title company will look for it.

  • A mortgage company that escrows taxes does not remove the owner's responsibility. The Treasurer says the owner is ultimately responsible, whatever arrangement exists with a bank or escrow company.
  • Late tax does not hurt your credit score, because the Treasurer does not report to credit bureaus.
  • Payments are accepted by mail, at the Treasurer's office, at listed collector banks through the second due date, or online. Credit card payments carry a 2.5% charge or a $2.00 minimum.

sections.h2: What is the appeal route for a St. Clair County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the tax bill, then the property record card, and confirm you are getting every exemption you qualify for. The assessed value is one-third of the estimated fair market value, and the Assessor bases that estimate on recent sales of similar homes by age, size and construction. If the card has an error, such as the wrong square footage (the Assessor measures the outside perimeter of the house), call the Assessor first.

If an informal review does not fix it, you can file with the three-member Board of Review at 10 Public Square, Belleville, IL 62220. The 30-day filing window opens when the Assessor revises assessments. Evidence can include an exterior photo of your property and three comparable ones, property record cards, or a recent appraisal, sales contract, settlement statement or deed. Evidence must reach the Board at least five days before your hearing or the appeal is upheld unchanged. A decision can then be taken to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

A second route is a Tax Objection Complaint with the Circuit Clerk, usually used for a tax rate challenge. It must be filed within 75 days of the second installment due date.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can lower a St. Clair County tax bill?
sections.html:
The Assessor and Treasurer list several homestead programs, and a buyer or heir should check whether any carry over. The general homestead exemption applies to owner-occupied homes, and veterans, returning veterans and people with disabilities have their own exemptions. For seniors, the county lists three programs.

  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption: lowers the assessed value by $5,000 for a residence owned and occupied by someone 65 or older.
  • Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze: for owners 65 or older with total household income of $75,000 or less who use the home as a principal residence. Call the Assessor at 618-825-2704.
  • Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral: for people 65 or older with household income under $75,000. The state pays the tax and recovers it with 6% annual interest when the property is sold or transferred, up to $7,500 a year. Applications are due by March 1 and the Treasurer provides forms at 618-825-2440.

Homeowners who keep taxes current and have the homeowner occupied exemption can use the Treasurer's monthly payment plan. Enrollment opens in August and payments begin in September, and the plan does not change any due dates.

sections.h2: How are St. Clair County taxes handled when a house sells?
sections.html:
Property tax is paid in arrears, so the seller owes tax for the part of the year they owned the home, and the closing statement normally credits the buyer for that share. The Assessor's office tells owners to check their closing papers for the proportionate allowance for months they did not own the property.

Before you sign a sale contract, get the Treasurer's payment history for the parcel and the status of the current-year bill. If the house is a probate property, a rental or a long-vacant inherited home, ask whether anything is delinquent or has gone to sale. The County Clerk handles tax sale questions at 618-277-6600, and the Board of Review at 618-825-2489 can answer exemption questions that affect the buyer's bill.

A cash buyer will want the same documents as any other buyer: the parcel number, the latest bill, and proof that exemptions are correct. Having them ready keeps the closing date from slipping.

faqs.q: How often are St. Clair County property taxes paid?
faqs.a: In two installments each year. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026 the Treasurer listed July 1 and September 1 as due dates. Ask the Treasurer's office for the next schedule, since every date on the published list is marked tentative.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying St. Clair County property tax late?
faqs.a: The State of Illinois imposes a 1.5% monthly penalty on the unpaid balance, and it increases by 1.5% every thirty days. The amount with penalty is printed on the payment coupon of your bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to challenge a St. Clair County assessment?
faqs.a: The Board of Review's 30-day filing window begins when the Assessor revises assessments. Evidence must reach the Board at least five days before the hearing. A tax rate challenge goes to the Circuit Clerk within 75 days of the second installment due date.

faqs.q: Can I redeem my property after a tax sale in St. Clair County?
faqs.a: Yes. If the property is your principal dwelling with no more than six apartment units, you can redeem for two and one-half years. Other property must be redeemed within two years. Redemption requires paying the tax plus penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Which office handles senior property tax relief in St. Clair County?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at 618-825-2440 for tax deferral forms, the Assessor at 618-825-2704 about the Senior Assessment Freeze, or the Board of Review at 618-825-2489 if you qualify for the $5,000 senior homestead exemption and do not see it on your bill.
